subject: history
title: Key Events in Civil Rights
welcome_lead: Today you'll walk through the protests, laws and turning points of the rights movements.
meta_desc: GCSE History Civil Rights events — Brown v Board, Selma, Sharpeville, Civil Rights Act.
final_note: You can now sequence the major events and laws of the civil rights era.

concepts.def: 1954 ruling that school segregation was illegal
1957 black students escorted into a white school
Peaceful occupation of segregated lunch counters
1965 US law removing barriers to black voting

walkthroughs.body_html:
In Brown v Board of Education (1954) the US Supreme Court ruled school segregation unconstitutional.

In 1957 federal troops escorted the Little Rock Nine into Central High in Arkansas. In 1960 students staged peaceful sit-ins at segregated lunch counters.

The March on Washington in 1963 drew 250,000 people. Martin Luther King Jr gave 'I Have a Dream'.

President Lyndon B. Johnson signed the Civil Rights Act in 1964 and the Voting Rights Act in 1965 after the Selma to Montgomery marches.

In Sharpeville (1960), South African police killed 69 unarmed black protesters.

The ANC turned to sabotage and Mandela was jailed in 1962. The Soweto uprising in 1976 against Afrikaans in schools brought global outrage and economic sanctions on the regime.

Brown v Board of Education

Loving v Virginia

options: Ended school segregation
Removed barriers to black voting
Founded the NAACP
Started the bus boycott

mcqs.q: How was the US civil rights movement achieved?
options: Lincoln ended segregation by signing the 14th Amendment.
Brown v Board ended slavery in the southern states.
Through decades of mass organising — NAACP legal work, grassroots campaigns, sit-ins, freedom rides — alongside leaders like King and Malcolm X.
Martin Luther King's 'I Have a Dream' speech ended segregation.

mcqs.q: What did Brown v Board of Education decide in 1954?
options: Rosa Parks was the lawyer who argued Brown v Board.
The Supreme Court ruled that 'separate but equal' schools were inherently unequal, overturning Plessy v Ferguson and beginning legal dismantling of school segregation.
Brown v Board ended slavery in the southern states.
Brown v Board of Education immediately desegregated all schools in America.

mcqs.q: Was Rosa Parks's refusal to give up her bus seat a spontaneous act?
options: Lincoln ended segregation by signing the 14th Amendment.
Rosa Parks was just a tired seamstress who refused on impulse to give up her seat.
No — Parks was a trained NAACP activist; the boycott was organised by long-standing civil rights networks that turned her arrest into a planned campaign.
Rosa Parks was the lawyer who argued Brown v Board.
